problems.issue: Cross-sectional blindness is structural: the backbone never lets stocks attend to each other (B is always a batch dim in both experts; pooling+head are per-stock; routing is per-day-constant). A +5sigma perturbation of one stock leaks <1e-5 into other stocks' scores. The model produces a ranking over a cross-section it literally cannot observe pairwise.
problems.why_it_matters: This is the single architectural cap on cross-sectional expressivity and exactly matches the established 'portfolio-blind' theory (MSE has diagonal Hessian => zero gradient on breadth/turnover). It pinpoints why every readout/pool/tau lever was null: those operate per-stock and cannot add cross-sectional structure. The only structurally-available lever is an explicit cross-stock operator (CrossStockBlock / stock_backbone / stock_expert), which is precisely the open frontier. Any new lever that stays per-stock is predicted dead a priori.

problems.issue: loss_weights {listmle:1.0, ic:1.0} are dead config — never read. Only w['mse']*l_mse + z-loss backprop. The config strongly implies a 3-way listmle+ic+mse objective, but listmle/ic are monitor-only.
problems.why_it_matters: A researcher reading work_flow.py would reasonably believe ranking (ListMLE) and IC are in the training objective and design experiments around them. They are not. This is a live trap for hypothesis design and explains why RankIC-shaped interventions underperform: the gradient is pure pointwise MSE. If a ranking signal is actually wanted, it must be added to total_loss (HARD CONSTRAINT permits aux regularizers), not just given a weight.

problems.issue: The 'MoE' router is per-day, not per-token: with day-shared macro, gate weights are byte-identical across all 300 stocks (std 6e-8). The router's only degree of freedom is which day/regime, time-vs-factor mixing — never which stock.
problems.why_it_matters: The MoE provides regime-conditional temporal/cross-factor mixing but contributes ZERO per-stock specialization. Diagnostics like router_layer_*_time_ratio are per-day scalars; 'expert collapse' analyses on the stock axis are meaningless. Capacity spent on the router/experts buys day-level adaptivity, not stock-level discrimination — relevant when accounting for why added capacity (gen-gap capacity-invariant) doesn't move RankIC.

problems.issue: tau (and its scale=0.5) only reweights an additive position embedding; it does not constrain the time expert's receptive field, which is full bidirectional self-attention over all T=8 steps.
problems.why_it_matters: Explains the durable 'tau mechanism real but benefit null' finding mechanistically: changing tau reshapes the positional-emphasis envelope, but the attention can already integrate all 8 steps, so the portfolio/ranking impact is structurally bounded to near-zero. Future tau work should not expect receptive-field gains; if a true horizon limiter is wanted it must gate the attention/tokens, not the pos table.

problems.issue: Model is ~0.20M params on ~870K daily-stock training samples of weak-SNR 5-day returns (RankIC~0.08 => R²~0.6%). 60.8% of params sit in the 2 MoE blocks that only buy per-day adaptivity.
problems.why_it_matters: Confirms the gen-gap wall is signal-limited, not parameter-limited: the model already has capacity >= extractable signal (finetune hurts valid = overfitting). Adding width/depth is predicted null (consistent with 'gen-gap capacity-invariant'). ROI is in changing the structure (cross-sectional coupling), not the size.

open_questions: Does the layer_summary market token (the only x-driven cross-stock path) carry any usable signal, or is it numerically inert? A leave-one-out ablation (router_use_layer_summary on/off, n>=3 seeds) would quantify whether even this weak coupling matters before investing in heavier cross-stock operators.

When use_readout_stock_attn / stock_backbone are enabled, the VALIDITY INVARIANT 'batch = exactly one trading day' must hold at train AND eval. Worth confirming FixedDailyBatchSampler + model_adapter._daily_chunk_max_bs never split or mix days, since a violated invariant would silently corrupt any cross-stock lever (the live frontier).

verified_facts.claim: Dispersion-anchoring / IC-maximization derivation is correct in form. Writing p=μ_p+s·z (z unit-variance, corr(z,y)=ρ=IC, y zero-mean std σ_y): L=μ_p^2+(s-ρσ_y)^2+σ_y^2(1-ρ^2). problems.why_it_matters: Substance is correct (the only label-coupled supervision on p is MSE), but anyone auditing should know there is a second active gradient (z-loss load-balancing) on shared weights. problems.issue: The std(p)*≈0.23 sanity number is contingent and partly circular. The derivation gives std(p)*=IC·σ_y exactly; '0.23' only holds if (a) the relevant IC≈0.23 and (b) σ_y≈1. 0.23 is far above the reported validation rank_ic 0.0786, so it would have to be the in-sample TRAINING Pearson IC — which is not verified from code. problems.why_it_matters: The functional law std(p)*=IC·σ_y and L*=σ_y^2(1-IC^2) are robustly correct, but the headline numeric should be tagged as a prediction requiring an empirical check (log std(p) and train Pearson IC), not an established fact. Confusing rank_ic with the Pearson IC that MSE actually optimizes is an easy error.

problems.issue: The 'label std≈1' assumption is only approximately true. CSZScoreNorm(method='robust') normalizes by MAD (×1.4826), pinning the MAD-scale to 1, NOT the standard deviation. With DropExtremeLabel absent (confirmed: not in learn_processors), the 5-day-return label keeps fat tails, so true σ_y > 1 (likely ~1.2-1.6).
problems.why_it_matters: σ_y>1 raises both std(p)*=IC·σ_y and the loss floor L*=σ_y^2(1-IC^2) above the '0.23' / '1-IC^2' figures. More importantly, untrimmed tails mean MSE's squared-residual weighting is dominated by a few extreme-label names per day — exactly the names where the robust-z transform did NOT clip — which biases the per-name gradient toward tail-fitting and is itself a portfolio-relevant distortion.

problems.issue: The portfolio-blindness claim is airtight for turnover/cost but overstated for breadth. Turnover and transaction cost are TEMPORAL functionals (p_t vs p_{t-1}); with one batch = one trading day (FixedDailyBatchSampler), no loss term ever sees two days jointly ⇒ literally zero cross-day gradient. Breadth (within-day concentration) is a functional of the joint daily score vector that separable MSE shapes INDIRECTLY through per-name ranks — it is not literally 'exactly zero gradient', it is 'no explicit breadth term; indifferent among equal-MSE configurations'.
problems.why_it_matters: The lever map should distinguish: turnover/cost = strictly orthogonal new gradient directions (MSE provably contributes nothing); breadth = a direction MSE touches weakly via IC, so a breadth/IR auxiliary partially overlaps the existing IC gradient and must be designed to add the dispersion-shaping component MSE lacks, not re-add IC.

problems.issue: Shift-sensitivity (∂L/∂c=2·mean(p)) and the diagonal Hessian can read as contradictory but are consistent and should be stated precisely: the common-mode penalty is a FIRST-ORDER effect arising because Σ∂L/∂p_i=2(mean(p)-mean(y)) with mean(y)≈0 (centered label), i.e. the sum of independent per-name residuals — NOT a Hessian off-diagonal. There is no second-order cross-name coupling.
problems.why_it_matters: Prevents the false inference that MSE's common-mode penalty implies it already does some cross-name/portfolio shaping. It does not: every coupling that looks portfolio-like reduces to independent per-name pulls toward a pre-centered label.

problems.issue: cs_ic_loss as an auxiliary is the canonical DOUBLE-COUNT and confirms the 'ic monitor-only loses nothing' design. Optimally-scaled MSE already equals σ_y^2(1-IC^2), so −IC (losses.py:7-26) pushes the same Pearson direction; adding it on top of MSE mostly removes scale/shift sensitivity that MSE handles for free.
problems.why_it_matters: Validates keeping ic at weight 1 in config harmless-but-inert, and warns against proposing a Pearson-IC auxiliary as a 'new' lever — it is redundant with the existing MSE gradient.

open_questions: Empirical check needed to close the std(p)*=IC·σ_y prediction: log the per-day std(p) of the trained head and the in-sample training Pearson IC. If train Pearson IC≈0.23 and std(p)≈0.23·σ_y, row-83's number is confirmed; if std(p) is much smaller, the head is under-dispersed (a real, separate failure mode MSE should have prevented).

Measure σ_y (true std of the robust-z label per cross-section). If σ_y≫1 due to untrimmed tails, re-evaluate whether enabling DropExtremeLabel (currently only in the comment, not in learn_processors) changes the MSE gradient's tail-domination — this is a cheap data-pipeline probe, not an architecture change.

Orthogonal objective-space levers that carry NON-zero gradient on portfolio quantities and do NOT double-count MSE's IC gradient: (1) turnover/transaction-cost auxiliary — strictly orthogonal because MSE is per-day-separable, but requires a cross-day state of yesterday's per-name scores (incompatible with the current single-day FixedDailyBatchSampler; needs an EMA/cache of prev-day p). (2) batch-IR / Sharpe auxiliary (plan C3) — functional of the joint daily vector, shapes dispersion/breadth; must be built to add the part IC does not (concentration), or it collapses into the IC gradient. (3) top/bottom-decile or tail-asymmetric auxiliary — targets the names actually traded (topk=30, n_drop=5); MSE weights by squared residual, not portfolio membership, so a membership-weighted term is orthogonal. Note ranknet_topbottom_loss already exists (losses.py:29-49) and is merely switched off (rank=0.0) — it is the cheapest available probe of this lever.

What is partial (not pure) double-count: listmle (Spearman-flavored ordinal) vs MSE (Pearson/linear) overlap on monotonicity but listmle adds mid-rank ordinal information MSE underweights; cs_ic_loss is the pure double-count. Decide whether the rank-aware frontier is worth re-opening given the readout-layer rank levers were already KILLED — but those kills were ARCHITECTURAL (readout placement), not LOSS-term ablations, so a loss-term rank/tail auxiliary on top of frozen MSE is not covered by the existing kill-log and remains untested.

Architectural complement to the loss analysis: because the loss is provably name-separable, the only way to express portfolio structure is to make p_i depend on p_j inside the network (CrossStockBlock C1, common-mode-free repeller). The objective stays MSE; the coupling must come from the architecture. This is consistent with row-83's conclusion and is the already-filed but unrun frontier (analysis/stock_expert/PORTFOLIO_ALIGNED_PLAN.md).

problems.why_it_matters: Every reported headline (best rank_ic 0.0786, IR 1.1-2.25) and every n=6 paired lever promotion (tau0.5, d1pma g0.12) is an in-sample estimate over a single 2.5-year window. Epoch cherry-pick alone adds ~0.0035 (post_peak_decay); seed cherry-pick (best-of-6 vs mean) adds ~1 std ~0.003; and the program-level multiple-comparison over dozens of levers inflates further. Forward (truly unseen) Rank IC is unmeasured and the kill-discipline ('n>=3 paired effects count') is being applied on the reporting set itself, so promotions can be selection artifacts.

problems.issue: PRIMARY TARGET MISALIGNMENT. The model trains plain MSE (level/calibration-sensitive, ~Pearson IC), selects checkpoints on Rank IC (ordinal, monotone-invariant), and is traded by a top-30-of-~300 long-only TopkDropout strategy (top-decile + turnover + tail). These are three different objectives. Rank IC weights the middle of the cross-section equally with the tails and is empirically NOT rank-consistent with IR across seeds.
problems.why_it_matters: Selecting on full-cross-section Rank IC neither matches the loss being minimized nor the portfolio that earns the money. A checkpoint with higher Rank IC can have lower IR (verified in the n=6 CSV). A selection target aligned to the strategy (top-k precision / NDCG@30 / rank-weighted IC, or directly IR) would change which epoch/seed/lever wins. This likely explains the durable finding 'RankIC != IR at promotion.'

problems.issue: loss_gap_last and valid_mse/valid_main are uninterpretable. Train MSE is on the CSZScoreNorm-robust label (std~1); valid MSE is on the raw 5-day return (std~0.03) because valid is forced to DK_I. The 'generalization loss gap' therefore reflects a ~30x label-scale mismatch, not over/under-fitting.
problems.why_it_matters: A reader (or an automated bottleneck note) using loss_gap_last to judge over-fitting or the gen-gap wall is reading noise dominated by label scaling. Any conclusion drawn about train/valid loss divergence from this diagnostic is invalid; only valid_rank_ic (rank-invariant) is trustworthy across the DK_L/DK_I boundary.

allLevers.title: Rank-normal regression target (CSRankNorm) in place of CSZScoreNorm(robust) — match the trained marginal to the selection metric and the DGP's rank-only signal
allLevers.mechanism: Change ONLY the train label transform in work_flow.py:105-108 learn_processors: replace CSZScoreNorm(method='robust') with a per-day cross-sectional rank-to-normal-score map (Qlib CSRankNorm, or a 3-line custom Processor in the existing module/utils/processors.py pattern that does y -> Phi^-1(rank_pct)). Main loss stays F.mse_loss(p, y) (losses.py:81), p unchanged. WHY: row-83 proves MSE maximizes Pearson IC = corr(p, y), so the SHAPE of y's marginal is what the gradient optimizes. The current robust-z target keeps true return SPACING inside the +/-3 MAD band, so per-name gradient ~ (p_i - y_i) is dominated by the largest-magnitude middle/near-tail returns — which for weak-SNR 5-day returns are mostly noise (forensic problem: untrimmed +46%/-37% valid tails, robust-z only clips at +/-3). A rank-normal target equalizes the gradient contribution by ORDER, making MSE optimize a Spearman-flavored objective (van der Waerden scores) — exactly the checkpoint metric (valid_rank_ic) and the rank-based TopkDropout portfolio. The listmle_loss docstring (losses.py:88) literally assumes 'label has already been a monotone rank transform', evidence this was the intended target.

This is orthogonal: same MSE, different y. It is also distinct from the open DropExtremeLabel card (h-20260610-001), which DROPS 2.5%/side of data; CSRankNorm is a full-data monotone transform that keeps every name and changes the gradient weighting, not the sample set.

allLevers.title: Inject the cross-sectional coordinate as deterministic INPUT features (per-day CS-rank/CS-z channels) — give the per-stock model the relative position it is graded on, without any cross-stock coupling
allLevers.mechanism: Add a feature-side processor that appends, per day, the cross-sectional rank-percentile (and/or CS-z) of a curated subset of the 158 Alpha factors as NEW input channels (computed on day-T data only -> point-in-time safe). The backbone, pooling and head stay byte-identical and per-stock; B remains a pure batch dim. WHY: the architecture forensic proves a +5sigma perturbation of one stock leaks <1e-5 into other stocks' scores — the model literally cannot observe the cross-section it is ranked on. But the features are time-series-normalized (RobustZScoreNorm fit on the train period, work_flow.py:95-97), i.e. each stock is scaled by its OWN history, never by today's peer distribution. So the relative coordinate that determines cross-sectional rank is absent from the inputs. A deterministic CS-rank channel hands the model 'this momentum is in today's top decile' directly, recovering the information that a cross-stock attention block would have to synthesize — but as a fixed precomputed input, so MSE's diagonal Hessian and the single-day-batch invariant are untouched.
allLevers.falsifiable_prediction: Adding CS-rank channels for the top-K most-used Alpha factors lifts valid RankIC by >= +0.005 paired at n>=3 (confirm n=6). KILL if flat within +/-0.003 — that would prove the train-period time-series normalization already puts every stock on a common scale dense enough to encode relative order, and the cross-sectional coordinate adds nothing.
allLevers.est_cost: ~0.6 GPU-day: a Qlib feature Processor (CSRankNorm on feature group restricted to a subset) + tokenizer num_alphas bump (auto via _init_net) + n=3-6 runs.
allLevers.why_not_already_killed: The KILLED cross-stock lever (h2_stockexp / CrossStockBlock, cross_stock_block.py:36) and warm-q were INTERNAL representational blocks that pass messages between stocks inside the graph and damaged IC_mean/IR. This adds ZERO inter-stock message passing — it is a deterministic, leakage-audited INPUT feature; the model stays exactly as per-stock as the killed-pool baseline. It is also distinct from factor-pool reweighting (which reweights existing tokens) because it adds genuinely new cross-sectional information not present anywhere in the input tensor.

allLevers.title: Beta-neutralize the regression TARGET (predict idiosyncratic alpha, not market-loaded return) — stop spending MSE gradient on the unpredictable forward market move
allLevers.mechanism: Train-only custom Processor: for each day, estimate trailing beta_i (e.g. 60-day OLS of stock return on the SH000300 index), regress the forward-return label cross-sectionally on beta_i, and replace the label with the residual (then rank/z-score). Eval (DK_I) labels stay raw. Main loss stays MSE on this residual target. WHY: the 5-day cross-sectional return decomposes as r_i = alpha_i + beta_i * R_mkt[T+1..T+5] + e_i. CSZScoreNorm already removes the LEVEL (the demeaned market average), but it does NOT remove the beta-DISPERSION: after demeaning, high-beta names still carry beta_i * (demeaned R_mkt), and on large-move days this term dominates the cross-sectional spread. R_mkt over the FORWARD window is the single biggest driver of return dispersion and is fundamentally unpredictable from day-T stock features, so MSE (and its IC ceiling = corr(p, y)) is capped by, and its gradient dominated by, this irreducible noise routed through high-beta names. Removing it raises the achievable IC on the predictable alpha and de-biases the gradient away from beta-proxy fitting; a long-only top-30 book that selects on alpha rather than beta should draw down less.
allLevers.target_metric: IR_wc up and MaxDD down (primary); RankIC-on-residual-label up (secondary). Raw-label RankIC may fall — that is expected, not a failure.
allLevers.falsifiable_prediction: Beta-neutral target lifts with-cost IR by a paired margin clearing p<0.1 at n>=3 AND reduces MaxDD, with held-out-day RankIC-on-residual up. KILL if IR_wc and MaxDD are both within seed noise at n=6, OR if raw-label RankIC drops with no IR/MDD compensation (means beta dispersion was already negligible after CS-demeaning, or the portfolio needs the beta tilt).
allLevers.est_cost: ~0.7 GPU-day: precompute trailing beta from cached price/index data + per-day CS-regression Processor + n=3-6 runs. Must be run through quant-leakage-audit first (label-side transform).
allLevers.why_not_already_killed: No lever in the entire ledger has ever altered the label's FACTOR STRUCTURE — every kill was architecture (readout/pool/experts/tau) or a marginal/tail transform. It is distinct from DropExtremeLabel (removes tail OUTLIERS) because it removes a SYSTEMATIC common factor across all names, not extremes. It is distinct from tau-unclamp (a temporal-emphasis knob with null portfolio edge) because it directly attacks the irreducible-noise component that caps IC, which the forensics identify as the forward market move.

allLevers.title: De-stacked batch-Sharpe (IR) auxiliary on the BARE g012 backbone — isolate the portfolio gradient from the dead readout
allLevers.mechanism: Add one aux term at the loss-aggregation seam quant_moe_model.py:688 (total_loss = w['mse']*l_mse + l_aux + l_reg + lambda_ir*ramp(step)*l_ir), driven purely by QIB_MODEL_OVERRIDES_JSON (no work_flow.py edit), with use_readout_stock_attn=FALSE (readout OFF). Inside forward, from the live (p,y) on finite rows: build a dollar-neutral, L1-normalized long-short book w_i=(p_i - mean(p))/(sum|p-mean(p)|+eps) (L1 scale-pin chosen because MSE already fixes std(p)~=0.23), per-day book return r_t = sum_i w_i*y_i, and l_ir = -r_t/sqrt(EMA_var + eps) where EMA_var is a detached running buffer over days. MSE weight stays 1.0; lambda_ir ramps 0->0.08. The Sharpe denominator down-weights days whose book return co-moves with the running variance, placing a positive gradient on bet-correlation / effective breadth — the wT-Sigma-w term MSE's diagonal Hessian provably cannot touch (IR=IC*sqrt(BR_eff)*TC). The L1 numerator overlaps the IC numerator, so the genuinely-new content is the risk-adjustment denominator, NOT a re-added IC term.

allLevers.title: Turn ON the existing top/bottom-K RankNet auxiliary, matched to TopkDropout K=30 (membership-aligned tail loss)
allLevers.mechanism: Zero-code probe: set loss_weights.rank=lambda (sweep {0.05,0.1,0.2}) and config.rank_topk=30 via QIB_MODEL_OVERRIDES_JSON. The wiring already exists — l_rank=ranknet_topbottom_loss(p,y,rank_topk) is built whenever w['rank']!=0 (quant_moe_model.py:660-661) and added to total_loss at :696-697. losses.py:29-49 computes softplus(p_bot - p_top).mean() over the K names with the highest and lowest LABELS, i.e. exactly the long/short book the strategy trades. MSE remains main. This puts a pairwise gradient ONLY on the traded tails, where top-k precision lives — orthogonal to uniform MSE, which weights every name by squared residual regardless of portfolio membership. Set rank_topk=30 to match topk=30 (n_drop=5 implies the effective traded set ~30-35).
allLevers.target_metric: top-30 precision / NDCG@30 up -> IR up; ICIR up
allLevers.falsifiable_prediction: n>=6 paired vs anchor: top-30 precision (fraction of predicted-top-30 in realized-top-decile) and IR_wc both rise with paired-t p<0.1, RankIC within +/-0.002, IC not below 0.0669. allLevers.why_not_already_killed: The rank-aware kills (factor-pool, time-readout, 3-expert, warm-q) were ARCHITECTURAL placement ablations; NO loss-term rank/tail auxiliary on top of frozen MSE has ever been ablated (the loss-forensics explicitly note this is outside the kill-log). allLevers.title: Turnover-penalty aux via leakage-clean id-keyed past-score EMA — the only available gradient on TC
allLevers.mechanism: Maintain a detached per-stock-id buffer w_prev[id] (EMA of yesterday's normalized weight), updated AFTER the optimizer step. Add l_to = mean_over_today's_names((w_t[id] - w_prev[id])^2) at quant_moe_model.py:688, total += lambda_to*l_to, lambda_to swept {0.02,0.05,0.1}, MSE main fixed. Because MSE is per-day additively separable and each batch is exactly one trading day (FixedDailyBatchSampler), the live objective has provably ZERO gradient on day-to-day turnover; this term is the sole mechanism that can reduce it. It directly targets the TC factor in IR=IC*sqrt(BR_eff)*TC and the with-cost collapse (IR_wc 1.75->1.03, MDD 2.4x) that is invisible in gross IC. Leakage discipline: the buffer reads only PAST scores (never y or future), and MUST be reset at every train/valid/test segment boundary (gate with /quant-leakage-audit before GPU spend, per the plan's R5 concern). Use unique-names-only weights to avoid the sampler's with-replacement duplicate inflation (sampler.py:72-75).
allLevers.target_metric: realized turnover down, with-cost IR up, MaxDD_wc shallower
allLevers.falsifiable_prediction: n>=6 paired vs anchor: realized portfolio turnover drops measurably AND IR_wc rises above 1.750 (paired-t p<0.1) AND MDD_wc not deeper than -0.076, while RankIC/IC within +/-0.002. KILL if turnover is statistically unchanged (the buffer gradient is inert) OR gross RankIC drops >0.002. Clean sub-result: if turnover falls but IR_wc does not lift, the with-cost wound was not turnover-driven.
allLevers.est_cost: ~6 from-scratch runs (~18 GPU-hr) + one /quant-leakage-audit (0 GPU) gate; +/quant-stress on any survivor (the honest with-cost read).
allLevers.why_not_already_killed: A turnover gradient has never existed in this codebase — MSE is per-day-separable and the batch is one day, so turnover is structurally in MSE's null space. Filed as plan rung R5 but UNRUN and stacked on the dead readout; here it is de-stacked to the bare backbone and the buffer is made leakage-clean with a mandatory segment-boundary reset (the exact gate the plan flags). It is label-free in its gradient, so zero double-count with MSE's IC.

allLevers.title: Within-day factor-neutral breadth regularizer ||X^T w||^2 — a single-batch breadth gradient using the 158 alphas as a risk model
allLevers.mechanism: Inside forward, both the score p[B] and the input feature matrix are live (B,T,N=x.shape at quant_moe_model.py:311). Take the last-step feature slice X = x[:,-1,:] -> [B,158] (already RobustZScore-normalized, ~unit scale per alpha) as a per-stock factor-loading proxy. Form the dollar-neutral book w=(p-mean(p)) and add l_neut = sum_f (sum_i w_i * X_{i,f})^2 / (||w||^2 * 158 + eps) = the book's normalized net exposure to the 158 alpha factors. total += lambda_neut*l_neut, lambda swept {0.01,0.03,0.1}. Minimizing it forces the score's implied long-short book toward FACTOR-neutral (low w^T Sigma w with Sigma~=X X^T), which raises BR_eff and cuts systematic drawdown. This is a genuine SINGLE-BATCH gradient on bet-correlation (no cross-day EMA needed, unlike Sharpe), it is LABEL-FREE (zero IC double-count), and it has no buffer so no leakage surface. MSE stays main.
allLevers.target_metric: MaxDD_wc down, IR up via sqrt(BR_eff)
allLevers.falsifiable_prediction: n>=6 paired vs anchor: the realized book's factor exposure ||X^T w|| drops, the BR_eff proxy rises, and MDD_wc is shallower than -0.076 with paired-t p<0.1, while IC stays within -0.002 of 0.0669. KILL if BR_eff rises but IC falls >0.002 (breadth bought by destroying signal) or if MDD does not improve at any lambda (the 158 alphas are not the relevant risk axes).
allLevers.est_cost: ~6 from-scratch runs (~18 GPU-hr); negligible compute overhead (one B x 158 matmul per batch).
allLevers.why_not_already_killed: No objective term has ever used the input feature matrix as a within-day risk model; all kills were architecture or label-coupled. It differs from the filed C1 contrast operator (a value-space ARCHITECTURE op shrinking 64-dim common mode) by acting directly on the realized long-short BOOK's factor exposure in objective space, and from the Sharpe aux by carrying a true single-batch correlation gradient with no cross-day state. No code/loss change; MSE training is byte-identical. This separates the overfit component (train-vs-held-out-train gap) from the regime-shift component (held-out-train-vs-2020-22 gap). The two diagnoses imply OPPOSITE fixes (more regularization/EMA vs train-period reweighting toward valid-like regime), so every gen-gap lever spent so far was aimed without knowing which.

If held-out-same-regime >= 2020-22 + 0.03, overfit is real and the regularization track survives.
allLevers.est_cost: ~0.3-0.5 GPU-day (n=3 short runs on a 2014-2018 window, no extra epochs)
allLevers.why_not_already_killed: Every killed gen-gap lever (capacity cap00-06, tau 357x, finetune, full_daily sampler) ASSUMED overfit and changed the MODEL; none ever held out same-regime days to TEST whether the gap is overfit vs distribution shift. allLevers.mechanism: work_flow.py:251-255 has open/close/min costs AND limit_threshold all COMMENTED OUT, so the backtest fills at price limits with default frictions; and the EVAL label is RAW 5-day return, untrimmed (max +46.5%, p99.9% +26%) because DropExtremeLabel is only a stale comment (work_flow.py:100-104 vs the actual learn_processors at 105-108). Tests whether the edge survives when you can only trade what is actually tradeable.

lever.title: Inject the cross-sectional coordinate as deterministic INPUT channels (per-day CS-rank/CS-z of top alphas) — give the per-stock model the relative position it is graded on, with zero cross-stock coupling
lever.mechanism: Add a feature-side, point-in-time Processor that appends per day the cross-sectional rank-percentile (and/or CS-z) of the top-K most-used Alpha factors as NEW input channels (computed on day-T data only). Backbone/pooling/head stay byte-identical and per-stock; B remains a pure batch dim; tokenizer num_alphas auto-bumps via _init_net. RELATED label-side alternative (lower priority): beta-neutralize the train target (S3) — trailing-60d beta_i, CS-regress the forward-return label on beta_i, train on the residual (then rank/z); eval label raw; loss stays F.mse_loss. Both require /quant-leakage-audit first.
lever.target_metric: CS-rank channels: RankIC up (>= +0.005). Beta-neutral alt: IR_wc up + MaxDD down (raw RankIC may fall, expected)
lever.rationale: S1-input (S2), with S3 folded as a related label-side alt. Survives because the architecture forensic proves the backbone is cross-sectionally BLIND (a +5sigma perturbation of one stock leaks <1e-5 into others' scores) AND features are time-series-normalized (each stock scaled by its OWN history, never today's peer distribution), so the relative coordinate that determines cross-sectional rank is literally absent from the input tensor. This hands it back as a fixed, leakage-audited input with ZERO inter-stock message passing — distinct from the killed CrossStockBlock/pool (representational coupling) and from factor-pool reweighting (adds genuinely new info, not a reweight of existing tokens); MSE's diagonal Hessian and the one-day-batch invariant are untouched. Ranked last because the benefit is the most uncertain (a single input channel may not overcome the per-stock processing bottleneck) and the beta-neutral alt carries a leakage surface plus a real risk that the portfolio needs the beta tilt.
lever.est_cost: ~0.6 GPU-day (CS-rank channels: Processor + tokenizer bump + n=3-6) / ~0.7 GPU-day (beta-neutral alt: trailing-beta precompute + CS-regression Processor + n=3-6), each gated by /quant-leakage-audit (0 GPU)
